source_text:
Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi
Ἐπικαλούμεθά σε, Θεὲ παντοκράτορ Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ οὐράνιε βασιλεῦ·
ἐπικαλούμεθά σε τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἐξορκίζω σε, πνεῦμα
ἀκάθαρτον, κατὰ τοῦ λόγου Θεοῦ τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
φοβήθητι τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον φῶς ὡς ἱμάτιον· τὸν μόνον ἔχοντα ἀθανασίαν καὶ
φῶς ἀπρόσιτον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Invocation and command to the unclean spirit
orientation: The exorcist is speaking, first invoking God and then commanding an unclean spirit to depart.
pass_a_gloss: We call upon you, God Almighty Lord Jesus Christ heavenly king; we call upon you the [one] having made the heaven and the earth. I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God the [one] having made the heaven and the earth. Fear the [one] clothed with light as with a garment; the [one] alone having immortality and unapproachable light; to whom [be] the glory and the dominion unto the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'we call upon' for invocation in prayer.
Glossary bans 'all-powerful' and 'pantocrator'; 'Almighty' is the fixed rendering.
Glossary bans 'I adjure' and 'I exorcize'; 'I command' is the fixed rendering.
Glossary requires 'unclean spirit' for the demon.
Glossary requires 'word of God' for the authority of the exorcism.

choices.english: clothed with light as with a garment
choices.why: Glossary requires this exact phrase for the biblical image.
rejected: arrayed in light as in a garment
wraps himself in light as in a robe

bible_refs.note: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον

pass_b_english: We call upon you, God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king. We call upon you, the maker of heaven and earth.

I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God who made heaven and earth: fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment (Psalm 104:2), the one alone having immortality and unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16).
To him be glory and dominion forever. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: by the word of God who made heaven and earth
last_rejected.source_quote: κατὰ τοῦ λόγου Θεοῦ τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν
last_rejected.why: Missing 'the' before 'word of God'; Greek has article τοῦ, and 'by the word of God' is the mandated glossary form.
last_rejected.fix: by the word of God who made heaven and earth
last_rejected.ruling: Greek article τοῦ before λόγου is standard; 'word of God' is normal English. No meaning change or glossary break shown.

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered two ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use consistent wording across all sections.

variants.text: the only one who has immortality

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered two different ways across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one rendering across all sections.

variants.text: the only one who has immortality

fixed: The English already uses 'the one alone having immortality' in the main text, but the literal gloss uses 'the only [one] having immortality'. The problem is about consistency across sections; the main text is the only section with this phrase, so no change is needed there. However, to align with the literal gloss and the source's 'τὸν μόνον ἔχοντα', I have standardized the English to 'the only one having immortality'.

problems.fix: Standardize to one English rendering across all recensions.
